主要内容: PepsiCo reported third-quarter earnings of $1.48 per share, exceeding analyst expectations of $1.43 per share. However, revenue fell short of estimates at $16.24 billion compared to the expected $16.31 billion. The company attributed the disappointing beverage sales in North America to declining store traffic and a colder summer, which reduced demand for Gatorade. CEO Indra Nooyi acknowledged that the company had overemphasized media spending and shelf space for new low-calorie brands at the expense of core brands like Pepsi and Mountain Dew. Despite these challenges, cost-cutting and productivity improvements helped PepsiCo beat earnings expectations. The North American beverage business revenue dropped to $5.33 billion from $5.52 billion a year earlier, with operating profit declining 10% to $817 million. PepsiCo plans to have at least two-thirds of its beverages with 100 calories or fewer by 2025. While its snack business, including Frito-Lay and Quaker Foods, grew by 3% and 1% respectively, the company faces challenges in the U.S. retail landscape. Internationally, PepsiCo saw organic revenue growth of 5% in Latin America, 6% in Europe and sub-Saharan Africa, and 9% in Asia, Middle East, and North Africa. Overall, third-quarter net income rose to $2.14 billion, or $1.49 per share, from $1.99 billion, or $1.37 per share, a year earlier. PepsiCo reported earnings that exceeded expectations, with a 6 percent increase in profit. The company raised its expected adjusted earnings per share growth from 8 percent to 9 percent, citing a likely smaller impact from exchange rate fluctuations. PepsiCo aims for core earnings per share of $5.23 in 2017, up from $4.85 in 2016. However, the company revised its full-year organic revenue growth target downward, projecting growth of about 2.3 percent, which aligns with its year-to-date growth rate, from a previous estimate of at least 3 percent. Revenue for the latest quarter reached $16.24 billion, slightly below the estimated $16.31 billion. Organic revenue growth for the quarter was 1.7 percent. A correction was made to note that PepsiCo expects full-year organic revenue growth to approximate its year-to-date growth rate of 2.3 percent. An earlier version also incorrectly spelled the name of analyst Kevin Grundy.
